content.title: About
content.content: Peanut soup is a traditional dish in Southeast Asian cuisines where peanuts form the base of a thick, aromatic broth. The peanuts give the soup a rich nutty flavor, creamy texture, and a subtle sweetness. It is usually prepared with shelled peanuts, vegetables, spices, and sometimes coconut milk or noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, although they are treated as nuts in cooking.
In Thailand and Vietnam, peanut soup is served as a light lunch or snack.
The peanut sauce used in the soup is often made from roasted peanuts, garlic, and chili for a spicy kick.
Traditional Thai "khao tom" is sometimes enriched with peanut paste to create a thicker consistency.
Peanut soup can be made vegan when no animal broth is used.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peanuts contain about 25 % protein, making the soup a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: Contains heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: These fats support cardiovascular health and help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Provides magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle, nerve, and bone function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The creamy texture and fiber content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common food allergens; reactions can be severe.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Peanut soup can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should limit foods high in oxalates.

items.title: Salt and spice levels
items.content: Excessive salt or hot chilies may be unsuitable for individuals with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, often accompanied by rice, noodles, or fresh herbs. Garnish with crushed peanuts, lime wedges, and cilantro. For a vegetarian version, use vegetable broth instead of meat stock.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; reheat gently and add fresh herbs before serving.
